from.rationale: Disputes the premise that existing regulation suffices, stating that technology may outpace existing regulations and that minimum standards and guidelines need to be developed.

to: The paper calls for clear minimum standards and guidelines, guidance on explainability and an expanded cybersecurity perimeter, and states that regulatory gaps could matter if technological advances outpace existing regulations; it reports that some jurisdictions found existing regulations sufficient and that regulators focus on governance and risk management “by way of new regulations or existing ones”. It does not state that existing frameworks broadly fail to cover AI or that a separate framework is needed.

from: A staff paper attributed to its authors. The paper reports both approaches among jurisdictions; its own policy statements call for new standards, guidance on explainability and an expanded cyber perimeter.
to: A staff paper attributed to its authors. Re-read under decision 18a: calls for standards and guidance in specific areas, which do not alone contest broad coverage; the paper states no view on whether existing frameworks broadly cover AI.

from.rationale: Disputes the premise that existing technology-agnostic frameworks broadly cover AI by stating they were not built for autonomous agents.

to: The speaker states that existing frameworks were not built to contemplate autonomous agents and that more sophisticated governance and accountability frameworks “may be needed”, framed as a question to keep asking about agents; she does not state that existing frameworks fail to cover AI broadly or that a separate AI framework is needed.

from: In a speech published on 30 June 2026, Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability at the Bank of England, said that existing, technology-agnostic regulatory frameworks were not built to contemplate autonomous agents and that more sophisticated governance and accountability frameworks may be needed.
to: In a speech published on 30 June 2026, Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability at the Bank of England, said that, as AI capabilities increase, “we must keep asking” whether existing, technology-agnostic regulatory frameworks remain sufficient, that they were not built to contemplate autonomous agents, and that more sophisticated governance and accountability frameworks may be needed.

from: The speaker frames it as a question to keep asking and says new frameworks “may be needed”; she does not propose specific AI-specific rules. Compare her speech of 31 October 2024 (am-u12-boe-2024-breeden-engaging-machine).
to: Re-read under decision 18a: a question and a possible adaptation for autonomous agents, not a contest of broad coverage. She does not propose specific AI-specific rules. Compare her speech of 31 October 2024 (am-u12-boe-2024-breeden-engaging-machine).

from.rationale: The report accepts that existing regulations apply but disputes that they are sufficient, holding that AI-specific additions and guidance are needed.

to.rationale: Beyond incremental additions to existing regulations in named areas (which alone would not contest U12 under decision 18a), the committee recommends a dedicated framework for responsible and ethical AI adoption, including a dedicated institutional framework to issue financial-sector-specific standards, which disputes that AI needs no separate framework.

from: The report of the FREE-AI Committee placed on the Reserve Bank of India's website in August 2025 states that, despite existing regulations, there are incremental AI aspects that those regulations need to incorporate to be comprehensive, and that a comprehensive issuance on these aspects and on the applicability of existing regulations may be required.
to: The report of the FREE-AI Committee placed on the Reserve Bank of India’s website in August 2025 states that existing regulations need to incorporate certain incremental AI aspects to be comprehensive, and sets as its objective a framework for responsible and ethical AI adoption, recommending a dedicated institutional framework in the financial sector to issue financial sector–specific standards, audit benchmarks and guidance.

from: A partial contest: the report also recommends guiding regulated entities on how existing regulations apply to AI. The committee's text, not stated by the RBI to be its policy.
to: A partial contest: the report also recommends guiding regulated entities on how existing regulations apply to AI. Re-read under decision 18a: the incremental additions in named areas alone would not contest broad coverage; the stance rests on the recommended dedicated framework. The committee’s text, not stated by the RBI to be its policy.

to.result: re-read: stance kept (contests), ground narrowed to the recommended dedicated framework; two passages added. Not checked by the other family before; in the short check of 2026-11-04.
